sections.section_title: Clinical Context and Index Presentation of a Failing Multilayer Aortic Bioprosthesis
sections.description: This section introduces the patient’s presenting symptoms, comorbidities, and longitudinal valve history, framing why this case is clinically important. It establishes the concept of lifetime management of aortic stenosis in a patient who has already undergone two transcatheter valve procedures and later presents with recurrent prosthetic valve dysfunction after treated prosthetic valve endocarditis.
subtopics: Initial presentation: exertional dyspnoea, chest discomfort, dizziness, and fatigue
Relevant comorbidities influencing procedural risk: hypertension, multivessel coronary artery disease, prior PCI, pacemaker, diabetes, COPD, and recurrent gastrointestinal bleeding
Original 2014 TAVI with a 27 mm Lotus valve for severe aortic stenosis
Structural valve deterioration leading to 2022 TAV-in-TAV with a 23 mm Evolut valve
Early haemodynamic response after the second TAVI, including ejection fraction improvement
Complication of the 2022 procedure: femoral pseudoaneurysm requiring open vascular repair
September 2022 prosthetic valve endocarditis due to Enterococcus faecalis with recurrent prosthetic dysfunction
Clinical status in 2024: severe restenosis plus moderate-to-severe intraprosthetic regurgitation in a patient with two overlapping transcatheter valves
Why this case matters: increasing frequency of redo TAVI and the emerging challenge of TAV-in-TAV-in-TAV

sections.section_title: Core Background Medicine: Structural Valve Failure, Prosthetic Valve Endocarditis, and the Challenges of Serial Redo TAVI
sections.description: This section provides the focused background needed to understand the case. It explains how transcatheter valves fail over time, how infective endocarditis can damage bioprosthetic valves, and why a third transcatheter valve creates unique anatomical and haemodynamic problems beyond those seen in standard redo TAVI.
subtopics: Modern indications for TAVI and why long-term survivors increasingly present with prosthetic valve failure
Mechanisms of transcatheter bioprosthetic dysfunction: structural degeneration, leaflet fibrosis, calcification, and mechanical restriction
How prosthetic valve endocarditis contributes to prosthesis failure even after microbiological cure
Definitions and clinical impact of restenosis, intraprosthetic regurgitation, and mixed prosthetic valve dysfunction
Prosthesis-patient mismatch: definition, haemodynamic consequences, and why it becomes more likely with serial valve implantation
Coronary obstruction risk in valve-in-valve and valve-in-transcatheter-valve procedures
Concepts of neo-skirt formation, valve-to-coronary distance, sinus of Valsalva dimensions, and coronary ostial height
Importance of commissural alignment for coronary flow preservation and future coronary reaccess
Why overlapping stent frames complicate expansion, leaflet motion, haemodynamics, and future interventions
Guideline perspective on prosthetic valve endocarditis: surgery as standard, but need for individualised management when surgical risk is prohibitive

sections.section_title: Diagnostic Workup and Clinical Reasoning: From Recurrent Symptoms to Procedural Feasibility
sections.description: This section walks through the stepwise evaluation used to determine the cause of the patient’s recurrent symptoms and to judge whether a third transcatheter intervention was possible and appropriate. Emphasis is placed on integrating echocardiography, microbiology, transoesophageal imaging, CT anatomy, and operative risk assessment.
subtopics: Establishing severe prosthetic valve dysfunction on transthoracic echocardiography
Interpretation of mean gradient, aortic valve area, indexed valve area, Doppler velocity index, and regurgitation severity in prosthetic valves
Use of the continuity equation for aortic valve area calculation in prosthetic stenosis
Recognition of mixed prosthetic valve disease: severe stenosis with concomitant regurgitation
Diagnosis of prosthetic valve endocarditis in 2022: fever, positive blood cultures for Enterococcus faecalis, and worsening heart failure
Assessing cure before reintervention: repeated blood cultures, clinical reassessment, TEE, and multislice CT showing no active infection
Role of TEE in excluding vegetations and paravalvular complications before redo intervention
Multislice CT evaluation of triple-valve anatomy, including minimum lumen diameter and frame interaction
CT-based estimation of coronary obstruction risk: coronary heights, sinus dimensions, valve-to-coronary distance, and anticipated neo-skirt
Risk stratification for surgery versus transcatheter therapy: EuroSCORE II, comorbidity burden, prior procedures, and technical hazards of explantation
Differential management options considered: surgery, conservative therapy, and third transcatheter valve implantation
How the team concluded that treated prior endocarditis was not a contraindication once infection was resolved

sections.section_title: Procedural Strategy for TAV-in-TAV-in-TAV: Valve Selection, Imaging Guidance, and Technical Execution
sections.description: This section explains how the intervention was planned and performed. It focuses on translating anatomical analysis into procedural choices, including access strategy, valve choice, implantation depth, ballooning strategy, and methods used to reduce the risks of coronary obstruction and severe prosthesis-patient mismatch.
subtopics: Heart team decision-making and shared decision-making in an off-label, high-risk case
Why a third TAVI was favored over surgery in this patient
Selection of the Acurate neo2 prosthesis: supra-annular design, frame profile, and expected haemodynamic advantages in narrow anatomy
Rationale for local anaesthesia and the chosen arterial access sites
Intra-procedural aortography to confirm baseline severe aortic regurgitation
Use of a Safari guidewire for left ventricular support
Purpose of balloon pre-dilation under rapid pacing in a multilayer prosthetic construct
Real-time confirmation of preserved coronary flow after pre-dilation
High implantation strategy at the level of the Evolut leaflets to optimize effective orifice area
How CT modelling informed leaflet alignment and implant depth
Commissural alignment techniques and their role in preserving future coronary access
Post-dilation strategy to improve valve expansion and flow dynamics without intentional frame fracture
Assessment of final result with aortography: valve position, coronary patency, and absence of residual regurgitation
Procedural pitfalls unique to TAV-in-TAV-in-TAV and how they were mitigated

sections.section_title: Outcomes, Interpretation of Post-Procedural Haemodynamics, and Clinical Lessons for Lifetime Valve Management
sections.description: This section reviews the immediate and 1-year outcomes, teaches how to interpret the early high residual gradient, and distills the broader lessons of the case for longitudinal management of structural valve disease. It links procedural success with follow-up surveillance and future planning in patients likely to outlive their first valve intervention.
subtopics: Immediate post-procedural assessment using VARC-3 concepts
Initial echocardiographic findings: no regurgitation but high mean gradient and severe prosthesis-patient mismatch
Why early post-implant gradients can be misleading or improve over time after complex redo TAVI
Potential mechanisms of later haemodynamic improvement: better leaflet motion, post-dilation effects, partial frame expansion, and improved central flow
One-month evolution: lower gradient, larger valve area, and reverse remodelling
Intermediate follow-up: symptom resolution, absence of heart failure, and no recurrent infection
One-year outcomes: sustained clinical benefit, stable valve function, preserved ejection fraction, and no endocarditis recurrence
How to surveil patients after serial transcatheter valve interventions: symptoms, echocardiography, and infection monitoring
Long-term unresolved issues: durability of triple-stented constructs and future coronary access limitations
Potential rescue strategies if this prosthesis fails: surgical explantation, valve fracture concepts, and BASILICA-type approaches
Key take-home lessons on patient selection, CT-guided planning, and anticipating a lifelong procedural trajectory from the first TAVI onward
